content:
- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early days of the forecast horizon.
- Forecasts tend to peak too early and overshoot, particularly after recent spikes in history.
- Model shows persistent bias toward higher values, suggesting underweighting of downward momentum or overconfidence in short-term trends.
- Mean reversion is not adequately captured — forecasts remain elevated longer than actual prices decline.
- Forecasts lag behind true values by 1–3 days in the early part of the horizon, then catch up or diverge again.
- Model reacts too aggressively to recent high values, failing to account for potential cooling or policy-induced corrections.
- Overshoots are more common in the first 5–7 days of the forecast, then gradually correct — suggesting model lacks smoothing or decay in trend persistence.
- Model underestimates the magnitude of downward corrections after spikes, especially in the 10–15 day range.
- Forecasts show less sensitivity to recent low values, implying insufficient downward bias adjustment.
- Model fails to account for seasonal or policy-driven price floor effects — often underestimating minimums or overestimating volatility in low-price zones.
